Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet.

Quick answers up front:
- We can provision a dedicated GPU pool sized for your sustained qps; need the token length distribution and concurrency per request to finalize SKU sizing.
- 99th percentile token latency SLAs are possible as a contracted SLO for reserved commits, but they require an explicit pool sizing + patrol/standing capacity for bursts (or a short burst credit we can attach).

Marissa — looping you, Marcus, and Vivek in. Marcus, can you confirm the rough GPU equivalent we'd recommend for 120 sustained / 300 burst and whether the KV/prefix cache will materially change that number? Vivek, Sarah included a competitor commercial term (20% + $75k). I'm proposing we consider a one-time onboarding credit + a competitive pricing match request to close this in the quarter.

Next steps: Marcus to provide an ops sizing + risk notes; Marissa to propose a commercial concession (discount + optional credit). If we land on a concession, Vivek — will need exec approver for any >$50k credits or exceptions to standard termination language.

Thanks,

Olga / Marissa — looked through Nexa_Demand_Calc.xlsx. High level:

- Workload: multimodal inference (text + small image prompts). Median token length ~ 120, peak batch sizes estimated at 8 concurrent streams per call.
- Recommendation: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs for the committed pool to hit ~120 sustained qps with headroom for short bursts to 300 qps for up to ~10 minutes if we enable burst credits.
- Caching: enabling prefix/KV cache for repeated prompt prefixes should reduce effective GPU load by ~18-25% depending on hit rate; our sizing above assumes moderate cache hit (20%). If Nexa can guarantee a higher reuse pattern, we could step the pool down to 6x equivalent.
- SLA risk: we can contract a 99th percentile token latency SLA for the committed pool only. For bursts that exceed the dedicated pool, we either: (a) honor latency by pre-authorized burst capacity (billed per-second), or (c) fall back to a slightly higher-latency variant model. Option (a) is preferred but requires a buffer of on-demand GPUs or a convertible reserved buffer.

I'll attach a short ops note after we finalize the commercial ask.

— Marcus
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Vivek / Aditya —

Recap: Nexa is asking us to match a competitor's 20% discount + $75k onboarding credit. Sizing looks to be 8x A100-equivalent committed GPUs with caching assumptions as Marcus noted.

Commercial proposal (internal):
- 12-month reserved commit on Dedicated pool (8x equivalent)
- 15% off list price (we are not at 20% without exec approval)
- One-time onboarding credit: $60,000
- Burst credit: 100 GPU-hours of on-demand burst per month (billed beyond that at standard on-demand)
- Acceptable legal: standard termination (30-day notice) but require procurement to accept a short carve-out for force-majeure.

Why this closes: it sits between the competitor ask and our pricing bands — gives Procurement a near-match while keeping annualized unit economics within our target for Q4.

Asks: Vivek/aditya — need exec approval for the $60k one-time credit (concession > $50k) and approval to sign off on the burst-credit SKU. Also confirm we're comfortable with the 12-month term cap.

I'll prep a concessions memo and a draft SOW if we get the green light.

Thanks,

Marissa / team — reviewed the ask. Approve the commercial path with the following executive conditions:

1) Approve the $60k one-time onboarding credit as the competitive match concession.
2) Approve the 15% discount on the 12-month reserved commit under the condition we insert a "competitive match" clause limiting further price erosion (I attached CompeteClause-1.docx).
3) Legal must review and accept a mutual termination language that preserves our ability to reclaim burst resources with 14 days' notice in the event of abuse; procurement has to sign this off.

Operational note: do not promise a hard 99th percentile SLA for bursts above the committed pool without specifying the burst credit model explicitly in the SOW. Marcus, work with legal to codify the burst buffer language.

I'll approve the concession as long as the SOW includes the CompeteClause-1 and the DocuSign packet is routed through the enterprise sales queue.
